attachments: attachment.begin (params conversationId, body {name, mime, size, sha256}) buffers one upload on the phone and answers data {uploadId, chunkBytes (12288), expiresInMs}; attachment.chunk (params conversationId, body {uploadId, offset, data}) appends one base64 chunk at exactly that offset and answers data {offset} as the length after the write; attachment.finish (params conversationId, body {uploadId}) verifies length and sha256 and writes the file into the open conversation's own working directory over the same SSH session every other remote command uses, answering data {attachmentRef, path, name, mime, size, sha256, source: mobile-upload} where attachmentRef is the absolute remote path and is used as the file path itself; attachment.abort (params conversationId, body {uploadId}) drops the local buffer and writes nothing to any host. Only the conversation that is open can be uploaded to, the local buffer lives under noBackupFilesDir and never in the product database or a system backup, and a file the host already holds is never replaced: the write moves to name-1.ext instead. 413 UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE for a size over 8 MiB or a chunk over 12288 bytes, 429 UPLOAD_LIMIT for too many uploads at once or a full local buffer, 409 UPLOAD_OFFSET_CONFLICT for a chunk that does not continue the upload, 409 UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE for a finish before every byte arrived, 422 UPLOAD_HASH_MISMATCH for content that does not hash to what was declared (the buffer is discarded), 422 INVALID_REQUEST for a name, type, size or hash the protocol cannot carry, 500 UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE when the phone cannot buffer the upload, 410 UPLOAD_EXPIRED for an unknown or timed-out upload, 409 CONVERSATION_SWITCHED when the conversation changed before the write, 502 REMOTE_WRITE_FAILED when the host did not take the file (the step that failed travels in error, and nothing half-written is left on either side), 501 ATTACHMENT_UNSUPPORTED when this host has no local upload store at all

question.answer: interactions.review with params conversationId and requestRef, body.answer (body.data accepted); a single_string form takes the text, a multi-field form takes one JSON object, and the answer is validated against requested_schema before it is sent; a successful answer is the state transition, because the answered question leaves the window and no further frame is published for it
question.answerable: only the newest question of the open conversation is answered; any other reference answers 409 NOT_PENDING and never reaches the agent, and a question whose schema this host cannot read answers 501 QUESTION_UNSUPPORTED

raw_events.content: one bounded, control-stripped line '[event type] title status raw' for every event the chat has no row of its own for

stream_events.usage: one agent usage report becomes one message.stream frame of type acp_context_usage with data {used, size, cost?}; a report this build cannot read keeps its bounded raw line, and usage.read answers the same numbers as its own route
stream_events.complete: the turn boundary becomes one message.stream frame of type finish with data {conversation_id, turn_id, status: finished, stop_reason, outcome}, and the same boundary is announced once as the named turn.completed event whether or not this host accepted the turn itself
stream_events.session_info: one agent session fact (a retitled session and the like) becomes one message.stream frame of type tips with data.type info, carrying the bounded raw line plus title, status and session_id
stream_events.resolved: a resolved interaction stays silent: the product's own bookkeeping row covers something the chat already drew while it was pending, and an approval that left the window is withdrawn through confirmation.remove
stream_events.unknown: every other event still becomes the bounded tips/info raw line, so nothing the agent sent vanishes

stream_frames: every frame in stream_events is carried as the renderer's own stream message on `message.stream`: {id, msg_id, type, conversation_id, turn_id, position, status, data}, where the event's own payload is `data` — the shape the renderer reads a live message from, keyed by that event's type. The rows messages.list, messages.before and messages.latest answer — and the `messages` array of a runtime.snapshot answer — keep that same payload under `content` instead, because the conversation list draws those history rows as they are; an event therefore has one shape per reader, and the two shapes are not interchangeable: a live frame carries no `content` and a history row is not a frame the chat appends. Both carry the same id and msg_id for that event (m<history key>), so a frame can be matched to the row it came from.
link_events: the open conversation's host link is published on the same event channel from the product's own reconnect bookkeeping, without a poll of its own: realtime.reconnected once the link is usable again (the name the renderer reconciles history and approvals on), realtime.disconnected while it is lost or waiting for the user, both with {conversation_id, host_id, state (connected, offline or needs_user), link_state, reconnected, needs_user}; a frame is published only when the kind of that state changes, and conversations.list reports the same fact per row as offline and link_state
local_network_permission: the renderer host asks for the nearby-devices grant from API 36 on and for local-network access from API 37 on, once, the first time an action has to reach a host over the LAN (detection.refresh, hosts.refresh, conversations.create, project.read, search.sessions, attachment.finish, terminal.open, terminal.command.start — a console connects to that host itself); until that grant is there those routes answer 403 LOCAL_NETWORK_PERMISSION_REQUIRED with the reason and the host shows the degraded access on its own surface, so a refusal is never silent and the action can be retried after granting — the upload steps that only buffer a file on this phone (attachment.begin, attachment.chunk, attachment.abort) reach no host and are never held back by it, and an upload the grant stopped stays buffered until it is finished or expires

challenges.read: GET /api/challenges -> data.challenge {id, host_id, host_name, kind, message, secret}, or null while no connection asks for input; kind is host_key, password or key_passphrase, host_id is null once that host is gone, and no credential is ever part of this payload
challenges.answer: POST /api/challenges/:challengeId/answer with body.answer; a host_key challenge continues on 'accept' and cancels on anything else, an omitted or empty answer cancels the request, and the answer is never stored, logged or echoed back; 409 CHALLENGE_NOT_PENDING for an id that is no longer the pending one

messages_before: GET /api/conversations/:conversationId/messages/before?before=<cursor>&limit=n loads one older page from the history store and answers it in the messages.list page shape, with has_more_after true because the caller still holds the newer part; 409 HISTORY_EXHAUSTED when the product holds no older page, 500 HISTORY_LOAD_FAILED when it cannot be read, 422 INVALID_CURSOR when the cursor is not in the loaded window
messages_send: POST /api/conversations/:conversationId/messages sends one text prompt through the open conversation: body.content plus body.files, body.sessions, body.inject_skills and body.loading_id; the answer is 202 with data {msg_id, turn_id, runtime}, beside 422 INVALID_CONTENT for empty or over-long text, 422 SESSION_REFERENCES_UNSUPPORTED, 422 SKILLS_UNSUPPORTED and 409 CONVERSATION_NOT_READY, TURN_BUSY, APPROVAL_PENDING or CONVERSATION_SWITCHED when that conversation cannot take a message. A message may name up to 16 files, each one either a string that is an absolute path (starting with `/`) or the reference `attachment.finish` answered with — `{kind: 'upload', path: '<absolute remote path>'}` — whose kind, when one is given, has to be `upload`, with at most 1024 characters and no control character; a reference this host cannot hand to the Agent answers 422 INVALID_FILE_REF (a project reference names a relative path in a workspace this host does not hold, so it is one of those refusals), more than 16 entries answer 422 TOO_MANY_FILES, and a path named twice is carried once. The accepted paths are appended to the user's own text as one block below it — a blank line, the title line, then one path per line — because this host's send path carries text alone: the file itself stays where the upload landed and the prompt only names it, so nothing claims the file was sent as content. That block counts against the same message bound as the text (8192 units and 24 KiB), and a prompt that no longer fits answers 413 MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE instead of sending shortened text, which only a message carrying files can answer because over-long text alone keeps answering 422 INVALID_CONTENT. A draft stays text alone: draft.save refuses any file list with 422 ATTACHMENT_UNSUPPORTED and says the attachment travels with the message instead.
conversations_create: POST /api/conversations creates one conversation on a saved host. The host is named as params.hostId or as body.host_id — the field the renderer's own new-conversation entry sends, with body.hostId accepted for the same value — and the Agent and the working directory are accepted as body.agent and body.cwd or as the same parameters; data is the created conversation row plus session_id (the Agent's own native id), agent, cwd and created=true; 404 HOST_NOT_FOUND, 422 AGENT_UNKNOWN or INVALID_CWD, 409 SESSION_CREATE_FAILED carrying the repository's own reason (a directory the host cannot use fails as itself), 409 SESSION_ID_UNKNOWN when the Agent returned no native id
terminal_open: POST /api/conversations/:conversationId/terminal or POST /api/hosts/:hostId/terminal opens the product's own SSH terminal for that target: the host starts its own console for that saved host with the command its terminal route runs there as that console's pending command, so the user sees that command and confirms it in the console before anything is typed into the session and a hand-over the user cancels runs nothing. data {host_id, host_name, agent, cwd, target, command, opened: true}, plus conversation_id and session_id on the conversation path, the command being the product's own terminal route command for this host's Agent target, built by ShellCommands.start and wrapped once for that target; opened is true only once that surface really started, and a start the system refused answers 500 TERMINAL_START_FAILED with the reason it gave instead of reporting an opened terminal. The target is one conversation — whose Agent, session id and working directory the host reads from its own index, so it does not have to be open — or one saved host, which has none of its own: its Agent is the Agent of the conversation this product holds for that host while there is one, otherwise the first Agent that host's probe found installed, and its directory is body.cwd, which replaces the conversation's own directory when the conversation path sends one; 422 INVALID_CWD without a usable body.cwd for a host target or for a non-string one, 422 TERMINAL_TARGET_UNKNOWN naming neither target, 409 WORKSPACE_UNKNOWN without a usable directory for a conversation, 409 AGENT_UNAVAILABLE for a host holding no Agent any probe found, 404 HOST_NOT_FOUND or CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND for an unknown target, 501 TERMINAL_UNSUPPORTED for a target this app has no shell entry for or a build with no terminal surface at all; no credential is ever part of this payload
terminal_command: POST /api/conversations/:conversationId/terminal/command or POST /api/hosts/:hostId/terminal/command -> the same answer as terminal_open, with the same body, the same directory rules, the same hand-over to the console and the same refusals: on this host one terminal route runs the Agent's own TUI, so the command is the ShellCommands.start command of that conversation or that host's Agent; the route is named separately so the caller can hand it to the terminal as the Agent's TUI rather than as a plain shell
hosts_refresh: POST /api/hosts/:hostId/refresh probes that host through the repository's refresh entry and rescans its session index; data {host_id, refreshed, sessions, detection}; 500 HOST_REFRESH_FAILED keeps the code and reason the repository reported
hosts_list: GET /api/hosts lists the product's own SSH hosts; every row carries id (`host-<id>`), nickname, hostname, port, username, protocol, os_type, agent_target, target, target_supported (true for every target this app can address, so every row answers true in this build — a Windows host's own target included; false is kept for a target with no entry in the app, which none is today), session_count (how many conversations the session index holds for that host, a real 0 when that index was never read) and detection {checked, agents[{id, state, executable, version, capabilities, error}]}, the capabilities being exactly what that host's probe declared and null until one answered. On a Windows host agent_target is `windows` (the Agent runs on Windows itself; the older `native` value on such a row means the same and is still answered), `wsl:<distribution>` (one distribution of that host) or a value nothing can address, and target is the shell context that follows from it — posix, wsl:<distribution> or windows-native; a windows-native host is really probed — its installations through the Windows lookup (`where`, whose answer is an absolute Windows path per Agent, with no version or protocol capability claimed, because nothing on that path was run) and its directories through PowerShell — an Agent the lookup did not find is reported as not installed rather than as a guessed path, and only an answer this app cannot read at all (no PowerShell on the host, or a line it cannot parse) is answered as state `target_unsupported` with error `windows_native_unsupported`. Starting an Agent on that target is refused by this build with that fact as its own reason — the launch line this app builds is POSIX text a Windows shell cannot read — and the terminal route refuses it the same way, 501 TERMINAL_UNSUPPORTED, instead of handing over a command that shell cannot run. hosts.create and hosts.update answer the same row
conversations_list: GET /api/conversations lists one row per indexed (host, agent, session); every row carries agent (the wire value of that session's Agent, which the sidebar's own Agent filter reads from the row), offline (true while the product holds a link state for that host that is not connected), link_state (connected, disconnected, retrying, needs_user or unknown when the product never observed that host), cached (true while the row comes from the index cache rather than a read of that host in this pass) and workspace {host_id, cwd} for grouping, beside the existing id, name, project_id, status, runtime and extra fields
search_sessions: GET /api/search?q=<query>&host_id=<hostId>&agent=<kind>&limit=<n> searches across conversations in the two ways this host can honestly search: the index's own title, preview and directory fields, and the content of the selected remote transcripts (one bounded, read-only scan per host). data {query, items, total, has_more, coverage}; one item is kind=index with conversation_id, title — the label the conversation list shows that row under, being the index's own title when it holds one and the identifiers that row really carries otherwise, because a row the product no longer holds has no title to borrow — host_id, agent, session_id, cwd, field (title, preview or cwd), snippet, source (remote or cached) or kind=content with the same identity fields plus title, snippet, file, line, anchor (file#line) and clipped, both carrying openable (false when that conversation is no longer held and cannot be opened from here); coverage {complete, truncated, failed_sources[{host_id, code: source_unreadable, reason}], problems[stable codes such as search_timeout or search_tool_missing], skipped[{conversation_id, host_id, agent, session_id, code}], roots, searched_sessions, index_complete, remote_rows, cached_rows} is false while any part of the range stayed unread, so a caller never renders it as a history without that text; 422 INVALID_QUERY for an empty, control-carrying or over-long query or an out-of-range limit, 404 HOST_NOT_FOUND and 422 AGENT_UNKNOWN for filters nothing could match, 500 SEARCH_FAILED when the search itself could not run; nothing is opened, sent or written by a search
inbox_list: GET /api/inbox is the read-only attention projection over the open conversation alone - the only one whose approvals, questions, failure and running turn this host holds - answered as data {items[{conversation_id, host_id, agent, session_id, reasons, pending_approvals, pending_questions, last_error, summary, updated_at}], total, read_only: true, scope: open_conversation}; a conversation reporting nothing has no row, an unreported time stays null, and this route approves, answers or changes nothing
queue_list: GET /api/queue answers every message the product still holds in its cross-conversation queue, oldest first, as data {items[{queue_id, host_id, agent, session_id, conversation_id, kind (notify or request), text, created_at, state, pending}], total, stats{stored, pending, delivered, withdrawn, dropped}}; state is the queue's own state for that row — pending, delivered or withdrawn — and pending is true only while it is pending, so a message its conversation took and one its sender withdrew stay readable as what they are instead of as still on their way, and only a pending row carries a withdrawal that can still happen; reading the queue sends and delivers nothing
queue_send: POST /api/queue with body.conversation_id, or body.host_id plus body.agent and body.session_id, plus body.kind (notify or request) and body.text queues one message for another conversation; the target must be a conversation the product already holds, the text must be non-empty and within the message bound; data {queue_id, conversation_id, host_id, agent, session_id, kind, state: pending, queued: true, delivered: false} claims only what is queued, because a request is delivered by opening that conversation and never here; 404 CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND for a target the product does not hold, 422 INVALID_KIND, 422 INVALID_CONTENT, 422 QUEUE_REFUSED when the queue itself refused the row, 500 QUEUE_UNAVAILABLE when it cannot be read or written
queue_cancel: DELETE /api/queue/:queueId withdraws one queued message so it can never be delivered later; data {cancelled: true, queue_id, state: withdrawn, delivered: false} never claims a delivery, and the product's queue keeps the message under its own terminal state `withdrawn`, so a withdrawn message is never handed to its conversation, is never counted as delivered, and does not come back as pending (the state literal in this round trip and in queue.list is always `withdrawn`); only a message that is still pending can be withdrawn — one its conversation already took belongs to that conversation, and one already withdrawn is ended — and both of those answer 409 QUEUE_NOT_PENDING because the queue still holds the row, it is simply not pending; 422 INVALID_QUEUE_ID for a malformed id, 404 QUEUE_NOT_FOUND for an id the queue does not hold at all
reference_pack: POST /api/conversations/:conversationId/reference builds one bounded context pack of that conversation's own loaded window through the same AgentSessionReference projection the Compose quote uses, as data {conversation_id, host_id, host, agent, session_id, cwd, status (complete, trimmed or empty), text, quoted_count, omitted_count, cut_count, sent: false}; the text names what the window, the character budget and the item budget left out, and preparing a pack starts no model call; 409 CONVERSATION_NOT_OPEN when that conversation is not the open one or is not ready yet, 404 CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND for a conversation the product does not hold
index_clear: POST /api/index/clear drops the session index cache through the repository's own clear entry and answers data {cleared: true, sessions_before, sessions}, the second count being what the index holds afterwards; the confirmation a user must give is the front end's step, hosts, detections, drafts and the queue are separate stores, and 500 INDEX_CLEAR_FAILED keeps the code and reason the repository reported
